source.title: CAP: Co-Adversarial Perturbation on Weights and Features for Improving Generalization of Graph Neural Networks
source.authors: Hao Xue; Kaixiong Zhou; Tian-Long Chen; Kai Guo; Xia Hu; Yi Chang; Xin Wang

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether co-adversarial weight and feature perturbations affect GNN test performance and generalization gap using different interventions and measures from the listed versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports GNN test-performance comparisons, ablations, skip-epoch results, loss landscapes, and a generalization-gap comparison. Its perturbation-based GNN results do not test the specific label-memorization, width, convolution-versus-fully-connected, optimizer, batch-size, dropout, magnitude-aware-sharpness, or memorized-example-removal versions.
record.test_reason: The study uses the proposed connection between flat minima and generalization to motivate CAP and evaluates its performance on graph node classification. It tests none of V1–V8. Its closest comparison to V7 uses layer-norm-scaled random directions and cross-entropy loss landscapes, rather than magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance before training error rises; it also does not compare generalization-measure rankings.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that alternating weight and feature perturbations, following an initial standard-training stage, smooth GNN loss landscapes, shrink the generalization gap and improve test performance. The explicit gap comparison is GCN on Pubmed; the broader benchmark tables report test performance.
record.recipe_differences: Studies graph neural networks using alternating adversarial weight and feature perturbations with a two-stage training scheme; it does not test the listed interventions or model settings.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset, GNN backbone, graph mini-batch sampling method, and the number of initial vanilla-training skip epochs affect reported test performance. The authors report FLAG's effect also varies by dataset.

fits_no_version.finding: CAP has higher mean test performance than vanilla training in all 12 reported backbone–dataset combinations. Gains range from 0.07 to 2.44 percentage points; uncertainty is reported without significance tests.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Alternating adversarial weight and feature perturbations can improve held-out node-classification performance of evaluated GNNs.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 1 and Sections 3.2 and 4.3 describe smoother layer-norm-scaled random-direction weight loss landscapes and smaller train–test gaps for CAP than vanilla GCN on Pubmed. These are cross-entropy landscape comparisons, not V7's training-error perturbation-tolerance measure.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For GCN on Pubmed, smoother normalized random-direction weight and feature loss landscapes accompany smaller generalization gaps across vanilla, FLAG and CAP training.

fits_no_version.finding: CAP improves mean GraphSAGE test ROC-AUC with Neighbor, Cluster and SAINT sampling, and its Pubmed accuracy varies with the initial standard-training duration.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: CAP's performance gains extend across tested graph samplers and depend on when adversarial training begins.

record.problems: The generalization-gap and loss-landscape comparisons in Figure 1 are described for GCN on Pubmed; the supplied text gives no numerical values for those plotted comparisons. Main benchmark results report test performance rather than train-test gaps. Ten runs are reported for benchmark experiments, but skip-epoch Table 5 gives no uncertainty.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 1 has no exact numerical values in the text for the train-test accuracy gap or landscape comparisons. Figure 3 attack robustness results are outside the listed versions and not included as rows.

untested.parts: Fixed random-label fitting versus natural-label held-out performance with the same architecture and recipe.
Test-error changes with width beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size changes at fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations that remove their penalty.
Adding or removing dropout, its dependence on training-set size, and its interaction with augmentation and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance before training error rises, its association with gaps among comparably fitted networks, and ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized training examples versus equally many random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: Replace the reader's tests/T2 classification with uses_without_test/T4. All 55 rows remain unlinked to V1–V8; their states do not imply that CAP's improvements are absent. The numerical entries match the supplied tables. Figure 1 is already declared in rows_left_out, and no unrecorded result tests a listed version.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width sweep beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its ranking of generalization gaps.
Removing examples the network memorizes most.
